Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE (REC-vc-jose-cose-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own. Quotations of other documents are checked against the copies README.md lists with their digests. INSTANCE: the decoded JOSE Protected Header (a JSON object) of the JWS that secures application/vc+jwt or application/vp+jwt (§3.1.1, §3.1.2), or of the Issuer-signed JWT of application/vc+sd-jwt or application/vp+sd-jwt (§3.2.1, §3.2.2). LEVELS. The root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules: a failure is non-conformance. A rule marked imported is a MUST of another document, named with the clause of this source that makes it bind. Anchors ending in -should add the SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED and NOT RECOMMENDED statements and include the MUST level by reference: a failure there is a deviation from a recommendation, to be reported as a warning, never as non-conformance. A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. PROFILES: #vc-jwt-should, #vp-jwt-should, #vc-sd-jwt-should, #vp-sd-jwt-should; the root is the MUST level of all four. CONDITIONAL rules on kid are #kid-present, #kid-absolute-url (MUST) and #kid-thumbprint-url (RECOMMENDED); they are not part of the root, because their conditions lie outside the header: cross-field-rules.derived.yaml says when to apply them. NON-NORMATIVE: §3.1.3, JOSE Header Parameters and JWT Claims, opens with “This section is non-normative.” (§3.1.3), line 361. No constraint here is drawn from its keywords (README.md, Findings). Header parameters other than those below are not restricted: RFC 7515 permits them and this source forbids none.
title: JOSE Protected Header of a JWS-secured or SD-JWT-secured credential or presentation (DERIVED)

alg.$comment: required, a string: imported from RFC 7515 §4.1.1, “This Header Parameter MUST be present and MUST be understood and processed by implementations.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.1), made binding by w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0012 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0017 (JWS) and, for the Issuer-signed JWT, by w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0027 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0033 through RFC 9901, whose §4.1 builds on a JWS. Not none, for an SD-JWT: imported, RFC 9901 §4.1, “It MUST NOT use the none algorithm.” (RFC 9901 §4.1). Not none, for vc+jwt and vp+jwt: inferred from “Issuers, Holders, and Verifiers MUST ignore all JWT Claims Sets that have no integrity protection.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0005), from w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0023, and from the sentence after w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0004, which says the setting “is used to communicate that a Verifiable Credential or Verifiable Presentation encoded as a JWT Claims Set has no integrity protection.” (§1.1.2.1) The comparison is exact: RFC 7515 §4.1.1 makes the alg value case-sensitive, so NONE is not none.

typ.$comment: RFC 7515 §4.1.9 (imported): the media type of the complete JWS. A string: inferred, since RFC 7515 calls it a media type value and names no JSON type. Its value is constrained only by the -should profiles.

cty.$comment: RFC 7515 §4.1.10 (imported): the media type of the payload. A string, inferred as for typ. Its value is constrained only by the -should profiles.

kid.$comment: RFC 7515 §4.1.4 (imported): “Its value MUST be a case-sensitive string.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.4) The rules of this source on kid (§4.1.1, §4.2) are #kid-present, #kid-absolute-url and #kid-thumbprint-url.

iss.$comment: §4.1.2 lets iss sit in the JOSE Header: “If iss is present in the JOSE Header, the JWT Claims, or the COSE Header, a verifier can use this parameter to obtain a JSON Web Key to use in the verification process.” (§4.1.2) (no keyword). RFC 7519 §5.3 (Replicating Claims as Header Parameters) and §4.1.1 (imported) make it a string: “The "iss" value is a case-sensitive string containing a StringOrURI value.” (RFC 7519 §4.1.1). Its value is compared with the payload's issuer by cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-01 and X-02 (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0066, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0067).

cnf.$comment: cnf may sit in the JOSE Header (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0068). Its value is a JSON object: RFC 7800 §3.1, which that sentence names, speaks of “Other members of the "cnf" object may be defined” (RFC 7800 §3.1) (imported).

vcJwtShould.description: application/vc+jwt, SHOULD level (§3.1.1). Includes the root.

typ.$comment: SHOULD: “The typ header parameter SHOULD be vc+jwt.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0013). Required at this level: a typ that is absent is not vc+jwt. Supporting: w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0008; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0009. Spelling (inferred): RFC 7515 §4.1.9, imported through the MUST that names [RFC7515], says “Per RFC 2045 [RFC2045], all media type values, subtype values, and parameter names are case insensitive.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.9) and “A recipient using the media type value MUST treat it as if "application/" were prepended to any "typ" value not containing a '/'.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.9), so vc+jwt, application/vc+jwt and any case variant name the same media type and all pass here; a value with media type parameters does not (the source names the bare type). RFC 7515 §4.1.9 also says “it is RECOMMENDED that producers omit an "application/" prefix of a media type value in a "typ" Header Parameter when no other '/' appears in the media type value.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.9); a producer writing application/vc+jwt deviates from RFC 7515, not from this source.

cty.$comment: SHOULD, checked only when cty is present, as the sentence says: “When present, the cty header parameter SHOULD be vc.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0014). Spelling as for typ (RFC 7515 §4.1.10, imported: “A recipient using the media type value MUST treat it as if "application/" were prepended to any "cty" value not containing a '/'.” (RFC 7515 §4.1.10)). The sentence after it carries no keyword and says “The content type header parameter is optional, and can be used to express a more specific media type than application/vc when one is available.” (§3.1.1); so a cty naming a more specific media type deviates here and may be justified, which this schema cannot know.

kidPresent.$comment: MUST level, CONDITIONAL: “kid MUST be present when the key of the issuer or subject is expressed as a DID URL.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0065). Apply only when that condition holds; the header alone does not show it, so this is not part of the root. cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-03 states the proxy condition a test can observe.

kidAbsoluteUrl.$comment: MUST level, CONDITIONAL on §4.2 applying (controlled identifier documents in use), on iss being absent, and on the issuer (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0072) or the holder (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0074) being identified as a [URL]: cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-04 and X-05. The pattern is inferred: a scheme, a colon and no whitespace, an approximation of an absolute-URL string of the URL Standard ([URL], C.1). That the URL names a verification method listed in a controlled identifier document or DID Document needs that document retrieved and is not checked here.

kidThumbprintUrl.$comment: RECOMMENDED (a warning), CONDITIONAL on URL identifiers being used: “When using [URL] identifiers, the kid is RECOMMENDED to be an absolute [URL] that includes a JWK Thumbprint URI as defined in [RFC7638].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0073). includes is read as contains (inferred). The URI form urn:ietf:params:oauth:jwk-thumbprint:<hash>:<value> is defined by RFC 9278 §3, not by [RFC7638], which the sentence cites and which defines no thumbprint URI (README.md, Findings). The example printed after the sentence passes.
